rows.stem: When Sodium bicarbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, the gas evolved is :

options.label: A
options.text: Hydrogen; it gives pop sound with burning match stick.

options.label: B
options.text: Hydrogen; it turns lime water milky.

options.label: C
options.text: Carbon dioxide; it turns lime water milky.

options.label: D
options.text: Carbon dioxide; it blows off a burning match stick with a pop sound.

rows.solution:
Sodium bicarbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to give sodium chloride, water and carbon dioxide:

\(\mathrm{NaHCO_3 + HCl \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O + CO_2}\)

Carbon dioxide turns lime water milky because insoluble calcium carbonate forms. It puts out a burning match stick; the pop sound is the test for hydrogen, not for carbon dioxide.

This is option (C) Carbon dioxide; it turns lime water milky.

rows.stem: When aqueous solutions of potassium iodide and lead nitrate are mixed, an insoluble substance separates out. The chemical equation for the reaction involved is :

options.label: A
options.text: \(\mathrm{KI + PbNO_3 \longrightarrow PbI + KNO_3}\)

options.label: B
options.text: \(\mathrm{2KI + Pb(NO_3)_2 \longrightarrow PbI_2 + 2KNO_3}\)

options.label: C
options.text: \(\mathrm{KI + Pb(NO_3)_2 \longrightarrow PbI + KNO_3}\)

options.label: D
options.text: \(\mathrm{KI + PbNO_3 \longrightarrow PbI_2 + KNO_3}\)

rows.solution:
The insoluble yellow solid is lead iodide. Lead nitrate is \(\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2}\) and lead iodide is \(\mathrm{PbI_2}\), so two KI are needed:

\(\mathrm{2KI + Pb(NO_3)_2 \rightarrow PbI_2 + 2KNO_3}\)

Check: K 2 = 2; I 2 = 2; Pb 1 = 1; \(\mathrm{NO_3}\) 2 = 2. The other choices use the wrong formula for lead nitrate or lead iodide, or are not balanced.

This is option (B) \(\mathrm{2KI + Pb(NO_3)_2 \longrightarrow PbI_2 + 2KNO_3}\).

rows.stem: A metal ribbon ‘X’ burns in oxygen with a dazzling white flame forming a white ash ‘Y’. The correct description of X, Y and the type of reaction is :

options.label: A
options.text: X = \(\mathrm{Ca}\) ; Y = \(\mathrm{CaO}\) ; Type of reaction = Decomposition

options.label: B
options.text: X = \(\mathrm{Mg}\) ; Y = \(\mathrm{MgO}\) ; Type of reaction = Combination

options.label: C
options.text: X = \(\mathrm{Al}\) ; Y = \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) ; Type of reaction = Thermal decomposition

options.label: D
options.text: X = \(\mathrm{Zn}\) ; Y = \(\mathrm{ZnO}\) ; Type of reaction = Endothermic

rows.solution:
Magnesium ribbon burns in oxygen with a dazzling white flame and forms a white ash, magnesium oxide. Two substances combine to form one, so it is a combination reaction:

\(\mathrm{2Mg + O_2 \rightarrow 2MgO}\)

This is option (B) X = \(\mathrm{Mg}\) ; Y = \(\mathrm{MgO}\) ; Type of reaction = Combination.

rows.stem: Acid present in tomato is :

options.label: A
options.text: Methanoic acid

options.label: B
options.text: Acetic acid

options.label: C
options.text: Lactic acid

options.label: D
options.text: Oxalic acid

rows.solution:
Tomato contains oxalic acid. (Methanoic acid is in ant and nettle stings, acetic acid in vinegar, and lactic acid in curd.)

This is option (D) Oxalic acid.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: Sodium hydroxide is termed an alkali while Ferric hydroxide is not because :

options.label: A
options.text: Sodium hydroxide is a strong base, while Ferric hydroxide is a weak base.

options.label: B
options.text: Sodium hydroxide is a base which is soluble in water while Ferric hydroxide is also a base but it is not soluble in water.

options.label: C
options.text: Sodium hydroxide is a strong base while Ferric hydroxide is a strong acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Sodium hydroxide and Ferric hydroxide both are strong base but the solubility of Sodium hydroxide in water is comparatively higher than that of Ferric hydroxide.

rows.solution:
An alkali is a base that dissolves in water. Sodium hydroxide dissolves in water, while ferric hydroxide is a base that does not, so it is not an alkali.

This is option (B) Sodium hydroxide is a base which is soluble in water while Ferric hydroxide is also a base but it is not soluble in water.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: The name of the salt used to remove permanent hardness of water is :

options.label: A
options.text: Sodium hydrogen carbonate (\(\mathrm{NaHCO_3}\))

options.label: B
options.text: Sodium chloride (\(\mathrm{NaCl}\))

options.label: C
options.text: Sodium carbonate decahydrate (\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\))

options.label: D
options.text: Calcium sulphate hemihydrate (\(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O}\))

rows.solution:
Washing soda, sodium carbonate decahydrate, removes the permanent hardness of water: it precipitates the calcium and magnesium ions as insoluble carbonates.

This is option (C) Sodium carbonate decahydrate (\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\)).

rows.stem: The electron dot structure of chlorine molecule is :

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram (A) as printed - an electron dot structure of two overlapping Cl atoms; see the attached figure.

options.label: B
options.text: Diagram (B) as printed - an electron dot structure of two overlapping Cl atoms; see the attached figure.

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram (C) as printed - an electron dot structure of two overlapping Cl atoms; see the attached figure.

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram (D) as printed - an electron dot structure of two overlapping Cl atoms; see the attached figure.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - all four options are drawn electron dot structures, each two overlapping circles labelled Cl with crosses for one atom's electrons and dots for the other's; the options ARE the figure, and the number of electrons drawn in the overlap and around each atom is the answer, so the placeholders below withhold it. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
A chlorine atom (2, 8, 7) has 7 valence electrons and needs one more to complete its octet. Two chlorine atoms each share one electron, so the molecule has one shared pair (a single bond), and each atom keeps three lone pairs (6 electrons) of its own.

The correct structure shows exactly one cross and one dot in the overlap, with six crosses around one Cl and six dots around the other, so that each atom has 8 electrons around it. That is the structure drawn in option (C).

rows.stem: Observe the following diagram and identify the process and its significance from the following options :

options.label: A
options.text: Evaporation : maintains water contents in leaf cells.

options.label: B
options.text: Transpiration : creates a suction force which pulls water inside the plant.

options.label: C
options.text: Excretion : helps in excreting out waste water from the plant.

options.label: D
options.text: Translocation : helps in transporting materials from one cell to another.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the process is identified only from the printed sketch of a tree (ground line, roots, trunk, branches and one leaf, with arrows and the labels Water, Leaf and Water vapour); the stem names nothing, and the path the arrows trace is withheld here because it is the answer. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
The diagram shows water absorbed by the roots, rising through the trunk to the leaf, and leaving the leaf as water vapour. Loss of water as vapour from the aerial parts of the plant is transpiration. It creates a suction force that pulls water up from the roots through the xylem.

This is option (B) Transpiration : creates a suction force which pulls water inside the plant.

rows.stem: Opening and closing of stomata is due to :

options.label: A
options.text: High pressure of gases inside the cells.

options.label: B
options.text: Movement of water in and out of the guard cells.

options.label: C
options.text: Stimulus of light in the guard cells.

options.label: D
options.text: Diffusion of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) in and out of the guard cells.

rows.solution:
Stomata open when water flows into the guard cells and they swell, and close when the guard cells lose water and shrink.

This is option (B) Movement of water in and out of the guard cells.

rows.stem: A cross between pea plant with white flowers (vv) and pea plant with violet flowers (VV) resulted in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny in which ratio of violet (VV) and white (vv) flowers will be :
rows.solution:
The \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are all Vv. Crossing them (\(\mathrm{Vv \times Vv}\)) gives VV : Vv : vv \(= 1 : 2 : 1\) in the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation.

The question compares only the pure violet (VV) plants with the white (vv) plants, so the ratio is \(1 : 1\). (Violet to white flowers as a whole is \(3 : 1\), because the Vv plants are violet too.)

This is option (A) 1 : 1.

rows.stem: In plants the role of cytokinin is :

options.label: A
options.text: Promote cell division.

options.label: B
options.text: Wilting of leaves.

options.label: C
options.text: Promote the opening of stomatal pore.

options.label: D
options.text: Help in the growth of stem.

rows.solution:
Cytokinins promote cell division, so they are found in high concentration where cells divide rapidly, as in fruits and seeds. (Wilting of leaves is caused by abscisic acid, and auxins and gibberellins help the stem grow.)

This is option (A) Promote cell division.

rows.stem: The number of chromosomes in parents and offsprings of a particular species undergoing sexual reproduction remain constant due to :

options.label: A
options.text: doubling of chromosomes after zygote formation.

options.label: B
options.text: halving of chromosomes after zygote formation.

options.label: C
options.text: doubling of chromosomes before gamete formation.

options.label: D
options.text: halving of chromosomes at the time of gamete formation.

rows.solution:
Each gamete gets only one chromosome of each pair, so it has half the number of chromosomes. When two gametes fuse at fertilisation, the zygote has the full number again, which keeps the number constant from parents to offspring.

This is option (D) halving of chromosomes at the time of gamete formation.

rows.stem: Two LED bulbs of 12W and 6W are connected in series. If the current through 12W bulb is 0.06A the current through 6W bulb will be :
rows.solution:
In a series combination the same current flows through every element, whatever its power rating. So the current through the 6 W bulb is also 0.06 A.

This is option (B) 0.06A.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem: The correct pattern of magnetic field lines of the field produced by a current carrying circular loop is :

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram (A) as printed - a magnetic field-line pattern around a current carrying circular loop; see the attached figure.

options.label: B
options.text: Diagram (B) as printed - a magnetic field-line pattern around a current carrying circular loop; see the attached figure.

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram (C) as printed - a magnetic field-line pattern around a current carrying circular loop; see the attached figure.

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram (D) as printed - a magnetic field-line pattern around a current carrying circular loop; see the attached figure.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - all four options are drawn field-line patterns around the same circular loop (leads marked + and -, an axis marked N and S); the options ARE the figure, and which pattern and arrow sense is drawn in each is the answer, so the placeholders below withhold it. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
Near each point where the wire crosses the plane of the page, the field lines are concentric circles around the wire. Towards the centre of the loop the circles grow larger, and at the centre the lines are nearly straight, all passing through the loop in the same direction (given by the right-hand thumb rule for the current shown).

The pattern that shows all of these, circles around both parts of the wire and lines through the centre running the same way, is option (C).

rows.stem: The resistance of a resistor is reduced to half of its initial value. If other parameters of the electrical circuit remain unaltered, the amount of heat produced in the resistor will become :

options.label: A
options.text: four times

options.label: B
options.text: two times

options.label: C
options.text: half

options.label: D
options.text: one fourth

rows.solution:
The heat produced is \(H = I^2Rt\), which can also be written \(H = \dfrac{V^2t}{R}\).

The marking scheme takes the potential difference across the resistor as the quantity that stays unaltered. Then \(H = \dfrac{V^2t}{R}\), so halving R doubles the heat.

The wording "other parameters remain unaltered" is open to a second reading: if the current were kept the same instead, \(H = I^2Rt\) would make the heat half. With the potential difference fixed, as the marking scheme reads it, the heat becomes two times, which is option (B) two times.

rows.stem: An alpha particle enters a uniform magnetic field as shown. The direction of force experienced by the alpha particle is :

options.label: A
options.text: towards right

options.label: B
options.text: towards left

options.label: C
options.text: into the page

options.label: D
options.text: out of the page

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the directions are given only in the drawing: four parallel arrowed lines labelled Magnetic Field and one arrowed line labelled alpha-particle crossing them; the direction of the field and of the particle's motion is withheld here because it decides the answer. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
The field lines point to the right and the alpha particle moves down the page. An alpha particle is positively charged, so the direction of its motion is the direction of the current.

By Fleming's left-hand rule (forefinger along the field, to the right; middle finger along the current, down the page), the thumb points out of the page.

This is option (D) out of the page.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Reaction of Quicklime with water is an exothermic reaction.

**Reason (R) :** Quicklime reacts vigorously with water releasing a large amount of heat.
rows.context: Q. No. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reasoning based questions. These consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: (A) is true but (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: (A) is false but (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Quicklime (calcium oxide) reacts vigorously with water to form slaked lime, releasing a large amount of heat, so the reaction is exothermic:

\(\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq)}\) + heat

The Assertion is true, and the Reason is true and explains it, because a reaction that releases heat is by definition exothermic. This is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** In humans, if gene (B) is responsible for black eyes and gene (b) is responsible for brown eyes, then the colour of eyes of the progeny having gene combination Bb, bb or BB will be black only.

**Reason (R) :** The black colour of the eyes is a dominant trait.
rows.context: Q. No. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reasoning based questions. These consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: (A) is true but (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: (A) is false but (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Black eyes (gene B) are dominant and brown eyes (gene b) recessive, so BB and Bb give black eyes, but bb gives brown eyes. The Assertion, that all three combinations give black eyes, is false.

Black eye colour is the dominant trait, so the Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The inner walls of the small intestine have finger like projections called villi which are rich in blood.

**Reason (R) :** These villi have a large surface area to help the small intestine in completing the digestion of food.
rows.context: Q. No. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reasoning based questions. These consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: (A) is true but (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: (A) is false but (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The inner wall of the small intestine has many finger-like projections called villi, which are richly supplied with blood vessels. The Assertion is true.

The villi increase the surface area for the absorption of digested food, which is then taken into the blood. They are not there to complete digestion, so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** A current carrying straight conductor experiences a force when placed perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field.

**Reason (R) :** The net charge on a current carrying conductor is always zero.
rows.context: Q. No. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reasoning based questions. These consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: (A) is true but (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: (A) is false but (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A current-carrying straight conductor placed perpendicular to a magnetic field experiences a force (its direction given by Fleming's left-hand rule). The Assertion is true.

A current-carrying conductor has as many positive charges as negative ones, so its net charge is zero. The Reason is true.

But the force arises because of the moving charges (the current) in the field, not because the net charge is zero. Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
A student took a small amount of copper oxide in a conical flask and added dilute hydrochloric acid to it with constant stirring. He observed a change in colour of the solution.

(i) Write the name of the compound formed and its colour.

(ii) Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction involved.
rows.solution:
(i) Copper(II) chloride (cupric chloride, \(\mathrm{CuCl_2}\)) is formed. The solution turns blue-green.

(ii) \(\mathrm{CuO + 2HCl \rightarrow CuCl_2 + H_2O}\)

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: The industrial process used for the manufacture of caustic soda involves electrolysis of an aqueous solution of compound ‘X’. In this process, two gases ‘Y’ and ‘Z’ are liberated. ‘Y’ is liberated at cathode and ‘Z’, which is liberated at anode, on treatment with dry slaked lime forms a compound ‘B’. Name X, Y, Z and B.
rows.solution:
X is sodium chloride (NaCl); its aqueous solution (brine) is electrolysed in the chlor-alkali process. Y, at the cathode, is hydrogen (\(\mathrm{H_2}\)). Z, at the anode, is chlorine (\(\mathrm{Cl_2}\)). B is bleaching powder (\(\mathrm{CaOCl_2}\)).

\(\mathrm{2NaCl(aq) + 2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2NaOH(aq) + Cl_2(g) + H_2(g)}\)

\(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CaOCl_2 + H_2O}\)

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem:
Name the part of brain which is responsible for the following actions :

(i) Maintaining posture and balance

(ii) Beating of heart

(iii) Thinking

(iv) Blood pressure
rows.solution:
(i) Maintaining posture and balance: cerebellum (hind-brain).

(ii) Beating of heart: medulla (hind-brain).

(iii) Thinking: cerebrum (fore-brain).

(iv) Blood pressure: medulla (hind-brain).

rows.stem:
Where are auxins synthesized in a plant ? Which organ of the plant shows :

(i) Positive phototropism

(ii) Negative geotropism

(iii) Positive hydrotropism
rows.solution:
Auxins are synthesised at the tip of the shoot (the growing tips of shoot and root).

(i) Positive phototropism: the shoot (stem).

(ii) Negative geotropism: the shoot (stem).

(iii) Positive hydrotropism: the roots.

rows.stem:
Write one specific function each of the following organs in relation with excretion in human beings :

(i) Renal Artery

(ii) Urethra

(iii) Glomerulus

(iv) Tubular part of nephron
rows.solution:
(i) Renal artery: brings blood containing nitrogenous wastes into the kidney.

(ii) Urethra: passes urine out of the body.

(iii) Glomerulus: filters the blood, so that water, salts, glucose, urea and other small molecules pass into Bowman's capsule.

(iv) Tubular part of the nephron: selectively reabsorbs useful substances such as glucose, amino acids, salts and water from the filtrate.

rows.stem: Two green plants are kept separately in oxygen free containers, one in the dark and other in sunlight. It was observed that plant kept in dark could not survive longer. Give reason for this observation.
rows.solution:
Both plants are in oxygen-free containers, so neither can take oxygen from the air for respiration.

The plant in sunlight carries out photosynthesis, using carbon dioxide and water and releasing oxygen. It uses this oxygen for respiration, so it survives.

The plant in the dark cannot photosynthesise, so no oxygen is produced. Without oxygen it cannot respire aerobically and get enough energy, so it does not survive long.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
Observe the following diagram and answer the questions following it :

(i) Identify the defect of vision shown.

(ii) List its two causes.

(iii) Name the type of lens used for the correction of this defect.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the defect exists only in the drawing: three parallel light rays (dashed at their far ends) entering an eye ball through the eye lens, with Light rays, Eye lens, Retina and Eye ball labelled; where the rays meet relative to the retina is the quantity under test and is withheld here. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
(i) The parallel rays from a distant object meet in front of the retina, so the defect is myopia (near-sightedness, short-sightedness).

(ii) The two causes are excessive curvature of the eye lens, and elongation of the eyeball.

(iii) It is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens of suitable power.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The colour of clear sky from the earth appears blue but from the space it appears black. Why ?
rows.solution:
The particles in the earth's atmosphere are smaller than the wavelength of visible light, so they scatter light of shorter wavelength, the blue end of the spectrum, much more than red. This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all directions, so the sky looks blue.

In space there is no atmosphere, so there are no particles to scatter sunlight. No scattered light reaches the eye from the sky, so it looks dark (black).

rows.stem: Use of several pesticides which results in excessive accumulation of pesticides in rivers or ponds, is a matter of deep concern. Justify this statement.
rows.solution:
Most pesticides are non-biodegradable, so they are not broken down. They are washed into rivers and ponds, absorbed by aquatic plants and animals, and enter the food chain.

At each higher trophic level the chemicals become more concentrated, because each organism eats many organisms of the level below. This is biological magnification. Since human beings are at the top of many food chains, the highest concentration accumulates in our bodies and harms our health, which is why it is a matter of deep concern.

rows.stem:
(i) While electrolysing water before passing the current some drops of an acid are added. Why ? Name the gases liberated at cathode and anode. Write the relationship between the volume of gas collected at anode and the volume of gas collected at cathode.

(ii) What is observed when silver chloride is exposed to sunlight ? Give the type of reaction involved.
rows.solution:
(i) A few drops of acid are added to increase the electrical conductivity of water (pure water conducts very poorly).

Hydrogen is liberated at the cathode and oxygen at the anode:

\(\mathrm{2H_2O(l) \xrightarrow{\text{electricity}} 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

The volume of gas at the anode to that at the cathode is \(1 : 2\): the hydrogen collected at the cathode is twice the volume of oxygen collected at the anode.

(ii) The white silver chloride turns grey, because it decomposes in sunlight into silver and chlorine:

\(\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Cl_2(g)}\)

It is a decomposition reaction brought about by light (photolytic decomposition).

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
(i) Suggest a safe procedure of diluting a strong concentrated acid.

(ii) Name the salt formed when sulphuric acid is added to sodium hydroxide and write its pH.

(iii) Dry \(\mathrm{HCl}\) gas does not change the colour of dry blue litmus paper. Why ?
rows.solution:
(i) The acid must always be added slowly to water, with constant stirring, never water to the acid. Mixing is highly exothermic; adding water to concentrated acid can make the mixture splash out and cause burns, or crack the container.

(ii) The salt formed is sodium sulphate, \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}\):

\(\mathrm{2NaOH + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + 2H_2O}\)

It is the salt of a strong acid and a strong base, so its solution is neutral, with pH = 7.

(iii) Dry HCl gas does not ionise without water, so it gives no hydrogen ions (\(\mathrm{H^+}\) or \(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\)). Without these ions it shows no acidic behaviour and cannot turn dry blue litmus red.

rows.stem:
(i) How does Paramecium obtain its food ?

(ii) List the role of each of the following in our digestive system :

(a) Hydrochloric acid

(b) Trypsin

(c) Muscular walls of stomach

(d) Salivary amylase
rows.solution:
(i) Paramecium is a unicellular organism with a definite shape. Food is taken in at a specific spot on its surface, and it is moved to this spot by the beating of the cilia that cover the whole cell.

(ii) (a) Hydrochloric acid creates an acidic medium in the stomach, which helps the enzyme pepsin act; it also kills microorganisms that enter with the food.

(b) Trypsin digests proteins.

(c) The muscular walls of the stomach mix the food thoroughly with the digestive juices (and push it forward by peristalsis).

(d) Salivary amylase breaks down starch into sugar.

rows.stem:
(i) What is double circulation ?

(ii) Why is the separation of the right side and the left side of the heart useful ? How does it help birds and mammals ?
rows.solution:
(i) In double circulation, the blood passes through the heart twice in each complete cycle: once through the right side to the lungs (pulmonary circulation) and once through the left side to the rest of the body (systemic circulation).

(ii) Separating the right and left sides prevents oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing, so the body gets a highly efficient supply of oxygen.

This helps birds and mammals, which have high energy needs and constantly use energy to maintain their body temperature.

rows.stem:
Define the following terms in the context of a diverging mirror :

(i) Principal focus

(ii) Focal length

Draw a labelled ray diagram to illustrate your answer.
rows.solution:
A diverging mirror is a convex mirror.

(i) Principal focus: the point on the principal axis from which rays parallel to the principal axis appear to diverge after reflection from the mirror. It lies behind the mirror.

(ii) Focal length: the distance between the pole and the principal focus of the mirror.

Diagram: draw a convex mirror with its pole P and principal axis. Draw three rays parallel to the principal axis falling on the mirror and reflecting so that they spread out. Produce the reflected rays backward with dotted lines behind the mirror; they meet on the axis at the principal focus F. Mark the distance PF as the focal length f, and put arrows on the rays.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: An object of height 10 cm is placed 25 cm away from the optical centre of a converging lens of focal length 15 cm. Calculate the image-distance and height of the image formed.
rows.solution:
For a converging (convex) lens, \(f = +15\) cm, \(u = -25\) cm and \(h = 10\) cm.

By the lens formula \(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\),

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{25} = \dfrac{5 - 3}{75} = \dfrac{2}{75}\), so \(v = 37.5\) cm.

Height of the image: \(h' = \dfrac{v}{u} \times h = \dfrac{37.5}{-25} \times 10 = -15\) cm.

The image is 37.5 cm from the lens on the other side, and 15 cm high; the negative sign shows it is real and inverted.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: The power of a lens is +4D. Find the focal length of this lens. An object is placed at a distance of 50 cm from the optical centre of this lens. State the nature and magnification of the image formed by the lens and also draw a ray diagram to justify your answer.
rows.solution:
\(f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{4}\) m \(= 0.25\) m \(= 25\) cm. The power is positive, so it is a convex lens.

The object is at 50 cm, which is twice the focal length (at \(2F_1\)). For \(u = -50\) cm,

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{25} - \dfrac{1}{50} = \dfrac{1}{50}\), so \(v = +50\) cm.

The image is at \(2F_2\): real and inverted, and of the same size, with magnification \(m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{50}{-50} = -1\).

Ray diagram: draw the object AB standing on the axis at \(2F_1\). From A draw a ray parallel to the axis, which after refraction passes through \(F_2\), and a ray through the optical centre O, which goes straight on. They meet at A' below the axis at \(2F_2\), so the image A'B' is real, inverted and the same size as the object. Draw arrows on the rays.

rows.stem:
(i) Why is an alternating current (A.C.) considered to be advantageous over direct current (D.C.) for the long distance transmission of electric power ?

(ii) How is the type of current used in household supply different from the one given by a battery of dry cells ?

(iii) How does an electric fuse prevent the electric circuit and the appliances from a possible damage due to short circuiting or overloading.
rows.solution:
(i) Alternating current can be transmitted over long distances without much loss of electrical energy (its voltage can be stepped up for transmission and stepped down for use).

(ii) The household supply is alternating current (AC), which reverses its direction periodically; in India it changes direction every \(\dfrac{1}{100}\) s (frequency 50 Hz). A battery of dry cells gives direct current (DC), which flows in one direction only.

(iii) A fuse is a wire of low melting point connected in series with the circuit. When a current larger than its rating flows, as in short-circuiting or overloading, the heat produced melts the fuse wire and breaks the circuit, so the excess current stops before it damages the circuit and the appliances.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: For the current carrying solenoid as shown, draw magnetic field lines and give reason to explain that out of the three points A, B and C, at which point the field strength is maximum and at which point it is minimum ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the points exist only in the drawing: a horizontal solenoid with arrowed leads and three marked points A, B and C; where each point sits relative to the solenoid (inside or outside, beside or beyond an end) decides which has the strongest and the weakest field, so their positions are withheld here. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
Draw the magnetic field lines of the solenoid. Inside it they are parallel straight lines along the axis; outside they curve round from one end to the other, like those of a bar magnet, one end acting as a north pole and the other as a south pole. Mark the direction of the current in the turns and of the field lines.

The field is maximum at A, which is inside the solenoid. There the lines are crowded together, because the fields of all the turns add up, and the field is strong and uniform.

The field is minimum at B, which is outside the solenoid beside its middle. There the field lines are far apart, so the field is weakest. (C, on the axis just beyond one end, is where the lines are still emerging from the end, so the field there is weaker than at A but stronger than at B.)

rows.stem: Write one difference between biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes. List two impacts of each type of the accumulated waste on environment if not disposed off properly.
rows.solution:
Difference: biodegradable wastes can be broken down by biological processes (by bacteria and other decomposers), while non-biodegradable wastes cannot be broken down in this way.

Impacts of accumulated biodegradable waste (any two): it gives a foul smell; it becomes a breeding place for flies, mosquitoes and other carriers of disease; it can pollute water.

Impacts of accumulated non-biodegradable waste (any two): harmful chemicals enter the food chain and are concentrated at each level (biological magnification); it affects the fertility of the soil; plastics clog drains and harm animals that swallow them.

rows.stem:
(i) Draw the structure of the following compounds :

(a) Butanoic acid

(b) Chloropentane

(ii) How are structure (i) and structure (ii) given below related to one another ? Give reason to justify your answer.

Draw one more possible structure for above case.

(iii) Differentiate between saturated and unsaturated carbon compounds on the basis of their general formula.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - part (ii) compares two printed structures, labelled Structure (i) and Structure (ii), each a branched saturated hydrocarbon drawn as a condensed structural formula with CH3 groups on bonds; they are not typed here, per the rule that structures are figures, and the relation between them is what (ii) asks. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(i) (a) Butanoic acid, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2COOH}\): a straight chain of four carbon atoms. The first three carbons carry three, two and two hydrogen atoms; the fourth carbon carries a double-bonded oxygen and an –OH group (the –COOH group).

(b) Chloropentane (1-chloropentane), \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_2Cl}\): a straight chain of five carbon atoms with single bonds, every carbon carrying hydrogen atoms (three on the first, two on each of the others), and a chlorine atom in place of one hydrogen on the end carbon.

(ii) Structure (i) is \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}CH(CH_3)_2}\) and structure (ii) is \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C{-}CH_2CH_3}\). Both have six carbon atoms and fourteen hydrogen atoms, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{14}}\). They have the same molecular formula but different structures, so they are structural isomers.

One more structure with the formula \(\mathrm{C_6H_{14}}\) (any one): hexane, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}CH_3}\); or a five-carbon chain with a \(\mathrm{CH_3}\) branch on the second carbon, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}CH_3}\); or a five-carbon chain with a \(\mathrm{CH_3}\) branch on the middle carbon, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH_2{-}CH_3}\).

(iii) Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) have the general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\): the number of hydrogen atoms is more than twice the number of carbon atoms. Unsaturated hydrocarbons have the general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}\) (alkenes) or \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n-2}}\) (alkynes): the number of hydrogen atoms is equal to or less than twice the number of carbon atoms.

rows.stem:
(i) What happens when a small piece of sodium is dropped in ethanol ? Write the equation for this reaction.

(ii) Why is glacial acetic acid called so ?

(iii) What happens when ethanol is heated at 443 K in the presence of conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) ? Write the role of conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) in this case.

(iv) Write an equation showing saponification.
rows.solution:
(i) Sodium reacts with ethanol, hydrogen gas is evolved (with effervescence) and sodium ethoxide is formed:

\(\mathrm{2CH_3CH_2OH + 2Na \rightarrow 2CH_3CH_2ONa + H_2}\)

(ii) Pure ethanoic acid has a low melting point, 290 K, so it often freezes during winter in cold climates and looks like ice (glacier). That is why it is called glacial acetic acid.

(iii) Ethanol is dehydrated and ethene is formed:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. } H_2SO_4,\ 443\ K} CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2O}\)

Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent: it removes water from ethanol.

(iv) Saponification is the conversion of an ester back into the alcohol and the sodium salt of the carboxylic acid, by an alkali:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5 + NaOH \rightarrow CH_3COONa + C_2H_5OH}\)

rows.stem:
(i) Name and explain the two modes of asexual reproduction observed in hydra.

(ii) What is vegetative propagation ? List two advantages of using this technique.
rows.solution:
(i) Hydra reproduces asexually by budding and by regeneration.

Budding: a bud develops as an outgrowth on the body because of repeated cell division at one specific site. The bud grows into a tiny individual, and when fully mature it detaches from the parent and becomes a new independent individual.

Regeneration: if the body of hydra is cut into pieces, each piece can grow into a complete organism. Specialised cells in the piece divide and form the different tissues and organs.

(ii) Vegetative propagation is the growing of new plants from vegetative parts of a plant, such as the root, stem or leaves, instead of from seeds.

Advantages (any two):

1. Plants raised this way bear flowers and fruits earlier than plants produced from seeds.

2. It allows propagation of plants such as banana, orange, rose and jasmine, which have lost the capacity to produce seeds.

3. The new plants are genetically similar to the parent plant, so they have all its characteristics.

rows.stem:
(i) How is electric current related to the potential difference across the terminals of a conductor ?

Draw a labelled circuit diagram to verify this relationship.

(ii) Why should an ammeter have low resistance ?

(iii) Two V - I graphs A and B for series and parallel combinations of two resistors are as shown. Giving reason state which graph shows (a) series, (b) parallel combination of the resistors.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - part (iii) is read off the printed graph: I on the vertical axis and V on the horizontal, no tick values, two straight lines A and B from the origin; their relative slopes are withheld here because they are the answer. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
(i) The electric current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends, provided the temperature stays the same (Ohm's law): \(V \propto I\), or \(V = IR\).

Circuit diagram: connect a battery (a few cells), a plug key, an ammeter, a rheostat and the conductor (a nichrome wire, the resistor) in series. Connect a voltmeter in parallel across the resistor. Mark the positive and negative terminals of the ammeter and the voltmeter, the positive terminal of each meter going towards the positive terminal of the battery, and show the direction of the current. (Instead of a rheostat, the number of cells can be changed one at a time.)

Close the key, note the ammeter reading I and the voltmeter reading V, then change the current with the rheostat and repeat. The ratio \(\dfrac{V}{I}\) comes out the same each time, which verifies the relationship.

(ii) An ammeter is connected in series, so the whole current flows through it. Its resistance must be low so that it does not change the current in the circuit, which it is measuring, and lets the maximum current flow.

(iii) For a V-I graph drawn with I on the vertical axis, the slope is \(\dfrac{I}{V} = \dfrac{1}{R}\), so a larger resistance gives a smaller slope.

(a) The series combination has the larger resistance, so it is graph A, the line with the smaller slope.

(b) The parallel combination has the smaller resistance, so it is graph B, the line with the larger slope.

rows.stem: Show the electron transfer in the formation of magnesium chloride.
rows.context:
The melting points and boiling points of some ionic compounds are given below :

| Compound | Melting Point (K) | Boiling Point (K) |
|---|---|---|
| \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) | 1074 | 1686 |
| \(\mathrm{LiCl}\) | 887 | 1600 |
| \(\mathrm{CaCl_2}\) | 1045 | 1900 |
| \(\mathrm{CaO}\) | 2850 | 3120 |
| \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\) | 981 | 1685 |

These compounds are termed ionic because they are formed by the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal. The electron transfer in such compounds is controlled by the electronic configuration of the elements involved. Every element tends to attain a completely filled valence shell of its nearest noble gas or a stable octet.
rows.solution:
Magnesium (2, 8, 2) has 2 valence electrons and chlorine (2, 8, 7) has 7. The magnesium atom transfers one electron to each of two chlorine atoms, so all three reach a noble gas configuration:

\(\mathrm{Mg \rightarrow Mg^{2+} + 2e^-}\)

\(\mathrm{2Cl + 2e^- \rightarrow 2Cl^-}\)

In the electron dot diagram, Mg is drawn with its two electrons and an arrow from each to one of two Cl atoms (each shown with its 7 electrons). The product is \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\) together with two \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\) ions, each in brackets with a complete octet, giving magnesium chloride, \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\).

rows.stem: List two properties of ionic compounds other than their high melting and boiling points.
rows.context:
The melting points and boiling points of some ionic compounds are given below :

| Compound | Melting Point (K) | Boiling Point (K) |
|---|---|---|
| \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) | 1074 | 1686 |
| \(\mathrm{LiCl}\) | 887 | 1600 |
| \(\mathrm{CaCl_2}\) | 1045 | 1900 |
| \(\mathrm{CaO}\) | 2850 | 3120 |
| \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\) | 981 | 1685 |

These compounds are termed ionic because they are formed by the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal. The electron transfer in such compounds is controlled by the electronic configuration of the elements involved. Every element tends to attain a completely filled valence shell of its nearest noble gas or a stable octet.
rows.solution: Any two: ionic compounds are hard solids (and somewhat brittle); they are generally soluble in water but insoluble in solvents such as kerosene and petrol; they conduct electricity in the molten state and in aqueous solution, but not as solids.

rows.stem: While forming an ionic compound say sodium chloride how does sodium atom attain its stable configuration ?
rows.context:
The melting points and boiling points of some ionic compounds are given below :

| Compound | Melting Point (K) | Boiling Point (K) |
|---|---|---|
| \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) | 1074 | 1686 |
| \(\mathrm{LiCl}\) | 887 | 1600 |
| \(\mathrm{CaCl_2}\) | 1045 | 1900 |
| \(\mathrm{CaO}\) | 2850 | 3120 |
| \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\) | 981 | 1685 |

These compounds are termed ionic because they are formed by the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal. The electron transfer in such compounds is controlled by the electronic configuration of the elements involved. Every element tends to attain a completely filled valence shell of its nearest noble gas or a stable octet.
rows.solution:
The sodium atom (2, 8, 1) has one electron in its outermost shell. It loses this electron to the chlorine atom and forms the sodium ion, \(\mathrm{Na^+}\), whose configuration (2, 8) is that of the nearest noble gas, neon:

\(\mathrm{Na \rightarrow Na^+ + e^-}\)

rows.stem:
**Give reasons :**

(i) Why do ionic compounds in the solid state not conduct electricity ?

(ii) What happens at the cathode when electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride ?
rows.context:
The melting points and boiling points of some ionic compounds are given below :

| Compound | Melting Point (K) | Boiling Point (K) |
|---|---|---|
| \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) | 1074 | 1686 |
| \(\mathrm{LiCl}\) | 887 | 1600 |
| \(\mathrm{CaCl_2}\) | 1045 | 1900 |
| \(\mathrm{CaO}\) | 2850 | 3120 |
| \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\) | 981 | 1685 |

These compounds are termed ionic because they are formed by the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal. The electron transfer in such compounds is controlled by the electronic configuration of the elements involved. Every element tends to attain a completely filled valence shell of its nearest noble gas or a stable octet.
rows.solution:
(i) In the solid state the ions are held in a rigid structure by strong forces of attraction, so they cannot move. With no movement of ions, the solid does not conduct electricity.

(ii) Hydrogen gas is liberated at the cathode.

rows.stem: Why an offspring of human being is not a true copy of his parents in sexual reproduction ?
rows.context: The most obvious outcome of the reproductive process is the generation of individuals of similar design, but in sexual reproduction they may not be exactly alike. The resemblances as well as differences are marked. The rules of heredity determine the process by which traits and characteristics are reliably inherited. Many experiments have been done to study the rules of inheritance.
rows.solution: In sexual reproduction, a male gamete and a female gamete, coming from two different parents, fuse. The offspring gets a combination of the DNA (characters) of both parents, so it shows variations and is not an exact copy of either parent.

rows.stem: While performing experiments on inheritance in plants, what is the difference between \(\mathrm{F_1}\) and \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation ?
rows.context: The most obvious outcome of the reproductive process is the generation of individuals of similar design, but in sexual reproduction they may not be exactly alike. The resemblances as well as differences are marked. The rules of heredity determine the process by which traits and characteristics are reliably inherited. Many experiments have been done to study the rules of inheritance.
rows.solution:
The \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation is the offspring produced directly by crossing the first set of parents; in it only the dominant trait is expressed.

The \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation is the offspring produced by crossing (or self-pollinating) the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants; in it both the dominant and the recessive traits are expressed.

rows.stem: Why do we say that variations are useful for the survival of a species over time ?
rows.context: The most obvious outcome of the reproductive process is the generation of individuals of similar design, but in sexual reproduction they may not be exactly alike. The resemblances as well as differences are marked. The rules of heredity determine the process by which traits and characteristics are reliably inherited. Many experiments have been done to study the rules of inheritance.
rows.solution:
Variations give some individuals of a population a chance to survive a change in their environment. If the niche of a population changes, a population of identical individuals could be wiped out completely; if variations are present, some individuals may be suited to the new conditions and survive.

For example, if the water of a population of bacteria living in temperate waters became warmer because of global warming, most of the bacteria would die, but a few variants resistant to heat would survive and grow further. So variations are useful for the survival of a species over time.

rows.stem:
Study Mendel’s cross between two plants with a pair of contrasting characters.

RRYY (Round Yellow) \(\times\) rryy (Wrinkled Green)

He observed 4 types of combinations in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation. Which of these were new combinations ? Why do new features which are not present in the parents, appear in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation ?
rows.context: The most obvious outcome of the reproductive process is the generation of individuals of similar design, but in sexual reproduction they may not be exactly alike. The resemblances as well as differences are marked. The rules of heredity determine the process by which traits and characteristics are reliably inherited. Many experiments have been done to study the rules of inheritance.
rows.solution:
The four combinations in the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation are round yellow, round green, wrinkled yellow and wrinkled green. The new combinations, not present in either parent, are round green and wrinkled yellow.

They appear because, when two or more traits are involved, their genes are inherited independently of each other, whatever combination they were in in the parents. So the trait for seed shape and the trait for seed colour separate and recombine in the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation.

rows.stem: Determine the speed of light in diamond if the refractive index of diamond with respect to vacuum is 2.42. Speed of light in vacuum is \(3 \times 10^{8}\) m/s.
rows.context: The ability of a medium to refract light is expressed in terms of its optical density. Optical density has a definite connotation. It is not the same as mass density. On comparing two media, the one with the large refractive index is optically denser medium than the other. The other medium with a lower refractive index is optically rarer. Also the speed of light through a given medium is inversely proportional to its optical density.
rows.solution:
Refractive index of diamond \(= \dfrac{\text{speed of light in vacuum}}{\text{speed of light in diamond}}\), so

speed of light in diamond \(= \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{2.42} = 1.24 \times 10^8\) m/s. (The marking scheme writes \(1.23 \times 10^8\) m/s, cutting off the decimals of 1.2397 rather than rounding them.)

rows.stem: Refractive indices of glass, water and carbon disulphide are 1.5, 1.33 and 1.62 respectively. If a ray of light is incident in these media at the same angle (say \(\theta\)), then write the increasing order of the angle of refraction in these media.
rows.context: The ability of a medium to refract light is expressed in terms of its optical density. Optical density has a definite connotation. It is not the same as mass density. On comparing two media, the one with the large refractive index is optically denser medium than the other. The other medium with a lower refractive index is optically rarer. Also the speed of light through a given medium is inversely proportional to its optical density.
rows.solution:
A ray bends more towards the normal in a medium of higher refractive index, so its angle of refraction is smaller there. Carbon disulphide (1.62) has the highest refractive index and water (1.33) the lowest, so the increasing order of the angle of refraction is:

carbon disulphide < glass < water.

rows.stem:
The speed of light in glass is \(2 \times 10^{8}\) m/s and in water is \(2.25 \times 10^{8}\) m/s.

(a) Which one of the two is optically denser and why ?

(b) A ray of light is incident normally at the water-glass interface when it enters a thick glass container filled with water. What will happen to the path of the ray after entering the glass ? Give reason.
rows.context: The ability of a medium to refract light is expressed in terms of its optical density. Optical density has a definite connotation. It is not the same as mass density. On comparing two media, the one with the large refractive index is optically denser medium than the other. The other medium with a lower refractive index is optically rarer. Also the speed of light through a given medium is inversely proportional to its optical density.
rows.solution:
(a) Glass is optically denser. Light travels slower in glass (\(2 \times 10^8\) m/s) than in water (\(2.25 \times 10^8\) m/s), so the refractive index of glass is greater than that of water.

(b) The ray goes into the glass straight, without bending (undeviated), because it falls along the normal: the angle of incidence is \(0^\circ\), so the angle of refraction is also \(0^\circ\). Only its speed decreases.

rows.stem: The absolute refractive indices of water and glass are \(4/3\) and \(3/2\) respectively. If the speed of light in glass is \(2 \times 10^{8}\) m/s, find the speed of light in (i) vacuum and (ii) water.
rows.context: The ability of a medium to refract light is expressed in terms of its optical density. Optical density has a definite connotation. It is not the same as mass density. On comparing two media, the one with the large refractive index is optically denser medium than the other. The other medium with a lower refractive index is optically rarer. Also the speed of light through a given medium is inversely proportional to its optical density.
rows.solution:
(i) \(n_{\text{glass}} = \dfrac{c}{v_{\text{glass}}}\), so \(c = n_{\text{glass}} \times v_{\text{glass}} = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 2 \times 10^8 = 3 \times 10^8\) m/s.

(ii) \(v_{\text{water}} = \dfrac{c}{n_{\text{water}}} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{4/3} = \dfrac{9}{4} \times 10^8 = 2.25 \times 10^8\) m/s.
